drop-typescript-3: Agents don't install or keep TypeScript 3.x, so no realistic task hits the old behavior.
test-mock-reexports: Agent-written test code and imports are the same before and after; fixture types from either import now match, which only removes type errors.
test-react-0.19: Agent-written test code is the same before and after; only install-time peer resolution changes, and the install error names the @data-client/react version to install. Custom Providers passed to makeRenderDataHook() are rare and forward managers to DataProvider, which accepts the function.
codemods-package: New package at its first release (minor takes it from 0.0.0 to 0.1.0); nothing existing changes behavior, so there is no old habit to fail on.
devtools-action-log: Only debugging agents read these dev-only globals, and they learn __DC__ from the data-client skills; no app code or shipped tooling depends on __DC_CONTROLLERS__, which was added in 0.16 and isn't something agents have memorized.
test-react-native-renderer: Agent-written test code is the same before and after; only which testing library must be installed changes, and Jest names the missing @testing-library/react-native package, so agents can infer the fix.
fetch-if-stale-promise: The old return type was a union of the data and a Promise, so typed agent code could only use it through await or a Promise check, and both still work: the Promise branch now always runs and resolves the same data. Only untyped or cast code that read fresh data synchronously breaks, and agents treat fetchIfStale() like TanStack's ensureQueryData() and await or .catch() it, which now also works on fresh data.
